concept.name: Daily pivot
concept.definition: A pivot point computed from the previous trading day's high, low, and close, applied to the current day's trading — the original floor-trader usage. On StockCharts' convention, pivots for 1- to 15-minute intraday charts use the prior day's data and remain fixed all day.
concept.intuition: Yesterday's H/L/C distill into today's map of where buyers and sellers are expected to contest control.
concept.mechanics: Computed at the start of the day as P = (prior day H + L + C)/3 with the standard derived S1/S2/R1/R2 levels; the levels do not change intraday and are used as bias filter (price above or below P) and as support/resistance references.
concept.formula: P = (H_prev_day + L_prev_day + C_prev_day)/3; S1 = 2P - H; R1 = 2P - L; S2 = P - (H - L); R2 = P + (H - L).
concept.failure_modes: Gap openings can start the day far beyond the pivot, making the levels irrelevant; quiet range days slice back and forth across P, generating noise.
concept.misconceptions: That daily pivots are intraday reversal guarantees; they are reference levels whose reactions must be confirmed.
concept.example: An index future closes at 5000 with a 5030 high and 4970 low; today's daily pivot set is P = 5000, R1 = 5030, S1 = 4970, watched on the 5-minute chart all session.
